newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico raises $930 mln mostly via bridge loans.
newsitem.headline: Mexico raises $930 mln mostly via bridge loans.

text.p: Mexico has raised $930 million mostly via a series of short-term bridge loans that will form part of the funding used to prepay $6 billion in medium-term notes, a Finance Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.

An earlier Finance Ministry press release explained that the $930 million was part of some $2.5 billion already raised for the prepayment but it did not fully explain it. "These are going to be short-term bridge loans," Alejandro Valenzuela, spokesman at the Finance Ministry, told Reuters.
He said the bridge loans had already been arranged with several different creditors, but he declined to reveal their names.
"We have actually locked very good short-term financing. It's going to make up the $2.5 billion," he said.
But he noted that because the loans are short-term they will later need to be refinanced in the markets.
In addition to the bridge loans, dollar revenues from government financial assets will make up the $930 million, Valenzuela said, though he said these were smaller amounts.
